title: 50,000 sure, or flip for a million? 10,000 players, 0 left.
description:
The viral poll: keep 50,000 for certain, or flip a fair coin for 1,000,000. Expected value says flip. Half a million on average is ten times the safe money.

10,000 seeded players take the flip. Then the winners are offered the same bet again, round after round. The coin stays fair and the multiplier never changes, so every single flip is still worth ten times the safe money.

Measured at seed 0:
- round 1: 5,064 still holding
- round 6: 170
- round 10: 8
- round 13: 0 of 10,000, pot 0
- the pot grew a mean 10.02x per round before it hit zero (min 5.71x, max 13.33x)
- expected value after 13 rounds: 10 trillion times the stake

Nothing is rigged. Every round the pot multiplies by about ten and the crowd halves, and a bet that is always worth taking on average turns out to be a bet nobody survives. The average is taken across players, not across rounds, and you only get to be one player.

The counts in the narration are the printed outputs of this exact run.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
